name: National Democratic Institute for International Affairs (NDI)
job-title: NDI Asia-Pacific Regional Specialist for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning
level: Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics/Social Sciences/ Development Studies or in another related field
description:
﻿Vacancy Announcement

Position: NDI Asia-Pacific Regional Specialist for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

Founded in 1983, the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs (NDI) is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization working to strengthen and expand democracy worldwide. NDI works with democratic institutions in every region of the world to build political and civic organizations, safeguard elections and promote citizen participation, openness, and accountability in government. Headquarters in Washington, DsociaC, and NDI maintain offices in over 70 countries on five continents. Its diverse workforce of employees from 75 countries is united in the belief that democracies promote economic growth and development more consistently and equitably than non-democratic political systems. NDI’s office in Nepal has been operational since 1994 and has since collaborated with the Parliament, political parties, government agencies and civil society.

Position Summary: This specialist guides the implementation of NDI programming and provides technical assistance to NDI staff in the Asia-Pacific region and headquarters in the areas of program design, monitoring, evaluation and learning (DMEL). This position is based in the Nepal and reports to the Nepal Country Representative and the NDI Asia-Pacific deputy regional director.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

With direction from Asia-Pacific regional leadership and country/ program leadership:

  • Provide technical guidance and support in the coordination and execution of DMEL activities and processes;
  • Support country and program teams with program design, monitoring and evaluation plans, data collection tools and processes, ensuring sound performance monitoring and evaluation systems and protocols;
  • Participate in and support operationalizing the monitoring and evaluation of program performance against established plans and indicators through data collection and analysis methodologies, instruments, and protocols;
  • Guide the analysis, visualization, and interpretation of program performance data to support its use in decision-making, donor reporting, and collaborative learning and adaptation. Help country and program teams execute analysis and review processes to support data-driven learning, adaptation, and interventions for necessary course corrections;
  • Participate in program assessments and evaluations. Guide program and country teams on the preparation of program performance and impact evaluations and reports;
  • Support preparations for learning discussions and reflections to identify evaluation recommendations and program management improvements;
  • Support implementation of regional learning sessions for cross-regional learning between program teams on best practices and evidence;
  • Help coordinate necessary training and resources for country and program teams to build regional DMEL knowledge and capacity as well as data collection and management competencies;
  • Develop and foster effective working relationships with country and program teams, and help facilitate collaborative and inclusive processes to identify and implement regional DMEL activities, and ensure alignment with broader institutional strategies and approaches;
  • Support DMEL for program development opportunities and processes;
  • Perform other duties as required by regional leadership.

EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in social sciences, statistics, evaluation, international development or other relevant discipline or equivalent experience.
  • A minimum of eight (8) years of experience in monitoring and evaluation, preferably in the field of democracy and governance, international development, social science, data analysis, or statistics, and with I/NGO experience.
  • Experience in the design of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, conducting qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis, and reporting performance results against key performance indicators. Experience in statistical modeling/analysis is a plus.
  • Expertise and competence in project monitoring and evaluation, preferably related to international development work and in one or more of NDI’s program areas: e.g., civil society strengthening, democratic political institution strengthening, elections, women’s political empowerment, political inclusion of marginalized groups, etc.

REQUIRED SKILLS

  • Demonstrated competency in qualitative and quantitative research/data collection and data analysis/management, including the use and management of databases and related modeling and report preparation, and experience with database management, preferably with experience with MS Excel, MS Access, or other monitoring and evaluation platforms;
  • Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, including routine data collection, data quality assurance, and promoting data for decision making and interventions/learning;
  • Experience in designing and using evaluation tools and methods such as surveys, interviews, focus groups, and research from secondary sources;
  • Knowledge and expertise related to international donor monitoring, evaluation, and learning requirements to support program life cycles, ensure compliance, promote accountabilities, and support progress reporting;
  • Fluency in English, and excellent written and oral communication skills to present information and respond to questions. Language skills in Asian languages are a plus;
  • Problem-solving skills for identifying problems, drawing conclusions, determining options for resolution, and recommending next steps;
  • Strong interpersonal skills and cultural sensitivity to interact effectively and diplomatically with individuals at all levels of the organization, as well as externally-both domestically and internationally with NDI partners, funders and other stakeholders;
  • Capacity to work effectively both independently and as a member of a team, as well as to provide guidance to others;
  • Strong organizational skills with a high level of attention to detail;
  • Strong working knowledge of PC-based word processing and spreadsheet applications and experience with Google Apps (Gmail, Calendar, Google Drive, G+, etc.).

COMMENTS:

The application deadline is October 19. To apply, please e-mail a CV and cover letter to asiarecruitment@ndi.org.

Short-listed candidates will be contacted. No phone calls, please!

Applicants need to possess work authorization to work in Nepal.

NDI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

name: WWF Nepal
description:
﻿WWF Nepal, the global conservation organization leading international efforts for a living planet, seeks applications from qualified Nepali candidates for the following full-time position. If you think you are an achiever and willing to work within a diverse team in a multicultural environment with commitment and passion for what you believe in, you are highly encouraged to apply.

Job Description

The Program Associate, Wildlife Trade Monitoring – Terai Arc Landscape and Conservation Program (TALCP) will be responsible for implementing wildlife crime control activities with a primary focus on INL-funded projects, along with other illegal wildlife trade (IWT) and regular TALCP-related activities under the direct supervision of the Program Co-Manager-TALCP and in coordination with WWF Nepal’s thematic experts. S/he works in close collaboration with Protected Areas and Division Forest Offices, Buffer Zone User Committees (BZUCs), Community Forest Coordination Committees (CFCCs), Community-Based Anti-Poaching Units (CBAPUs), and local NGOs/CBOs and TALCP partners to ensure effective planning, implementation, and reporting of project outcomes. This position will also need to support and facilitate the preparation of donor reports and ensure the donor reporting of the designated project, viz, INL and IWT. The position is based in the TALCP office, Kolhapur.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Planning and Program Implementation

2. Support for Livelihoods Program

3. Support for Campaigns & Awareness

4. Support for Data Collection and Report Preparation

5. Capacity Building

6. Coordination

7. Communication

8. Other Duties

Working Relationships:

Internal: Work closely with the TALCP team, Landscape Unit, Wildlife Trade Monitoring Unit, Livelihoods Specialist, Senior Officer-Conservation Education, and interact frequently with the program and operations unit.

External: Interacts frequently with government agencies, Local communities, Conservation partners, NGOs/CBOs, and non-conventional partners.

Qualifications

Knowledge: A bachelor’s degree in Forestry, NRM, Environment Sciences, or related fields with a sound knowledge of wildlife conservation and protected area system, including buffer zone program. Understanding of livelihoods, conservation education programs, including community involvement in wildlife crime control, and CBAPU are required.

Experience: At least 2 years’ experience in related fields of wildlife conservation, natural resource management, livelihoods, campaigns, and awareness. Should have a strong knowledge of wildlife and species issues, especially the protection of wildlife and the role of the community in biodiversity conservation, including CBAPU. It is essential that the individual is technically proficient and qualified in the field of conservation and spends at least 80% of the time in the field. Should have good experience and exposure in the sector of youth livelihood, technical training, coordination, linkages, along with social mobilization.

Skills and Abilities:

  • Must be able to work with minimal supervision, both in the field and in the office.
  • Knowledge of MS Office, having typing skills both in Nepali and English languages, and can use appropriate software for presentation to relevant stakeholders.
  • Good written and spoken skills in the English language.
  • Good understanding of current issues, especially having knowledge of environmental and conservation issues.
  • Willingness to stay in the field.

Additional Information

Visit  https://careers.smartrecruiters.com/WorldWildlifeFundInc1/nepal for more information and to apply.

Interested applicants are requested to apply for the position by 17:00 hours on October 14, 2025.  Only shortlisted candidates will be informed. 

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

WWF is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Please join us in our mission to save life on Earth.

name: Nepal National Dalit Social Welfare Organization (NNDSWO)
job-title: Executive Director (Part Time for NNDSWO's Central Office)
description:
﻿VACANCY 

ORGANIZATIONAL PROFILE

NNDSWO (1982) is a network based organization having its district chapters in 74 districts in Nepal. NNDSWO envisions an equitable and prosperous society free from all forms of discrimination, exploitation and poverty where human rights, social justice and dignity of all are equally respected. Its Mission is to 'eliminate caste-based discrimination and untouchability and empower people for dignified life'. Human rights, governance, education and livelihood are four core thematic programme areas of NNDSWO. Gender equality, conflict transformation, youth empowerment, and advocacy on inclusive DRR are major crosscutting themes. It has successfully managed projects on human rights, governance, education, adolescent empowerment, etc. in all regions of Nepal in partnership with a dozens of inter/national partners/donors.

Currently, we are seeking competent, committed and dynamic candidates for the following position:

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR– 1 (Part Time for NNDSWO's Central Office)

JOB SUMMARY

The Executive Director of NNDSWO is responsible for overall management function (both office and programme) of the organization. The Executive Director is a leader of management team and under supervision of National President. S/he is responsible for developing policy, plan, programmes, project and budgets of the organization. The Executive Director makes decisions regarding day-to-day administrative functions as well as implementation of the programme activities under the constitution, guidance of policy, directives, decisions of the executive board of the organization. 

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

Planning and project cycle management

  • Develop consolidated annual plan and budget of the organization in line with strategic plan of the organization.
  • Ensure annual plan and budget of all project are timely developed and submitted to partners.
  • Manage project cycle of all projects of organization and ensure proper design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation.
  • Ensure projects are implemented in efficient, effective and economic manner.
  • Ensure implementation, monitoring and donor reporting of the especially assigned projects.

Monitoring, evaluation and knowledge management

  • Provide leadership for M&E Unit, and develop result based M&E Framework and plans for various projects.
  • Manage baseline process, mid-term review, final evaluations and research works of the organization.
  • Guide team members to documented lesson learned of different projects.
  • Ensure reporting of all projects is done within deadline and standard quality.

Human resources management

  • Manage staff recruitment and induction process of the organization.
  • Carry out staff supervision and give guidance to all staff through mentoring and coaching.
  • Carry out staff appraisal, needs assessment and prepare training programmes.
  • Reporting to supervisor about progress and challenges of project and staffs every month.

Financial management

  • Ensure all policies and rules are being implemented and followed.
  • Ensure that financial reporting is accurate and prepared in accordance to donor guidelines and in line with the organizations policies
  • Ensure procurement planning and procedures of the organization is properly followed.
  • Ensure all financial transactions of the organization is done in line with laws, organizational policies and donor compliances.
  • Ensure auditing of the organization is carried out timely, and ensure adequate management response in audit findings.

Fund raising and proposal development

  • Lead fund raising team and develop proposals for external fund raising.
  • Develop proposal writing capacity of central, province and district team of the organization.
  • Initiate innovative and creative concepts of fundraising from both local and international resources
  • Make contacts with potential donors and popularize the work of NNDSWO to them.

Networking and coordination

  • Represent NNDSWO in meetings with other organizations and donor agencies.
  • Ensure good communication and coordination with donor agencies.
  • Coordinate organization in consortium and civil society platforms and alliances, 
  • Devise strategies working with diverse stakeholders including government.
  • Coordinate and Communicate to all with respect Human Rights, Gender and person with different ability friendly. 

Organizational development

  • Support board in drafting policies, improving systems and developing procedures and guidelines of the organization.
  • Improve in good governance practices and ensure transparency, accountability, inclusion, participation and gender issues.
  • Ensure the organization continually learns from experience and adopts its strategies to suit the changing environment.
  • Perform roles as outlined in the policies of the organizations.
  • Perform good role between executive boards and staffs. 
  • Respect organization's rules, regulations, objectives, instructions, culture, values, norms, ethic, diversity etc.
  • Self-motivated to work long term in Dalit and Marginalized issues   

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Completed Master's degree in social science or management disciplines.
  • Minimum of five years working experience in managerial position OR Three Years in Director position with progressive responsibilities.
  • Previous experience in developing successful proposals for external donor fund raising is required.
  • Proven experience of managing projects on diverse sectors especially in advocacy, human rights, governance, education and livelihood is essential.
  • Experience in strategic planning, consolidated budgeting and policy drafting in NGO context is desired.
  • Proven experience of managing project funded by bi-lateral and multi-lateral donor agencies including USAID, EU and DFID.
  • Experience of working in a network based organizations is preferred.
  • Experience of managing and leading the consortium based projects. 

OTHER COMPETENCE REQUIRED

  • Good understanding of socio-economic and political context of Nepal 
  • Good understanding of RBA, Advocacy, Dalit and women rights issues
  • Knowledge on local laws and compliances 
  • LFA, M&E and reporting skills
  • Planning and budgeting skills
  • Research and data analysis skills
  • Procurement management
  • Communication and coordination skills 
  • Problem solving, personal management and time management.
  • Presentation and facilitation skills.
  • Good command on computer application including MS Excel.
  • Fluency in Nepali and English both in written and spoken.
  • Good knowledge to make long term strategy plan, Annual Work and Budget, new policies, government rules and regulations etc.

name: Forward Looking
job-title: Terms of reference ToR for documentary  (Videography & Photography Service Provision)
description:
﻿﻿Terms of reference ToR for documentary

(Videography & Photography Service Provision)

1. INTRODUCTION

About Forward Looking (FL)

Forward Looking, an NGO working for the person with disabilities (PWDs) to improve their quality of life through education support and economic empowerment. It has been implementing the Education Support Project (ESP) with grant support from Felm, Nepal.

The project aims to contribute to create an environment for the access to quality education for PWDs. Through the interventions of this project activities, ultimately the persons with disabilities have improved their dignified life, self-reliance and increases equal access to development benefits and services. Children with disabilities (CWDs) have increased their reach to quality education in an accessible educational institution. Persons with disabilities have improved their socio-economic status in conducive environment to enjoy their rights. Institutional and organizational capacity strengthened for policy, advocacy and disability inclusive development. The project has implemented in Kathmandu, Lalitpur, Dhading, Gorkha, Kaski, Baglung, Banke, Kailali and Surkhet districts.

2. Objectives

The overall objective of this assignment is to:

  • Document project achievements, success stories, and key achievements through high-quality video and photographs.
  • Produce a short documentary film and a photo archive that can be used for reporting, advocacy, awareness, and promotional purposes.

3. Scope of Work

The selected service provider will be responsible for:

i. Videography

  • Shooting project achievement, interviews with beneficiaries, staff, and stakeholders.
  • Capturing both planned and field-based activities (training, meetings, home visits, etc.).
  • Editing and producing a professional documentary (10–20 minutes) and shorter clips (1–5 minutes) suitable for social media.
  • Including subtitles, background music, voice-over/narration, and branding (logo, captions with sign language.

ii. Photography

  • Capturing high-resolution photographs of beneficiaries, project interventions, and events.
  • Providing edited, captioned photos suitable for reports, publications, and social media.

iii. Deliverables

  • One full documentary film (10–20 minutes).2–5 short thematic clips (1–5 minutes each).
  • Minimum [X] high-resolution edited photographs with captions.
  • Raw footage and original photo files.

4 Time frame and location of the assignment:

  • The assignment will begin from 1st of November and terminate on 10th December. The specific activities have been provided below.
S. NActivitiesDatesRemarks
1Inception meeting and development of documentary and schedule1st November, 2025
2Submission of draft video (rough cut)End of November Includes text, visuals, layout and sign language
3Feedback from FL5 December, 2025Collaborative review
4Final submission video photo10 December, 2025 Assignment closure
  • Fieldwork will be conducted in Particular and potential areas of Kathmandu, Lalitpur, Dhading, Gorkha, Kaski, Baglung, Banke, Kailali and Surkhet districts.

5. Expected Outputs

  • Professional, rights-cleared, and ready-to-use documentary and photos.
  • Materials that reflect the voices and realities of beneficiaries with sensitivity, dignity, and inclusiveness.

6. Qualifications of Service Provider

The consultant/company should have:

  • Proven experience in professional videography and photography (portfolio required).
  • Experience working with NGOs, development projects, or social causes.
  • Technical expertise in video editing, subtitling, sound design and sign language.
  • Understanding of disability-inclusive communication will be an advantage.

7. Submission of Proposal

Interested applicants are requested to submit:

  • A brief technical proposal outlining methodology, work plan, and equipment.
  • Financial proposal with breakdown of costs.
  • Portfolio of previous similar work.
  • Profile/CVs of key personnel.

9. Payment Modality

  • Payment will be made in 2 installments – e.g., 40% upon signing contract, 60% after final approval of deliverables.

10. Submission of Technical and Financial Proposals

The potential and interested firms/consultants must submit technical and financial proposals sharing their keenness to conduct the Videography & Photography Service Provision of Forward Looking in the email address (thapasurya143@yahoo.com or info@flooking.org.np). The deadline for the submission of technical and financial proposals is 23rd October 2025. The documents required for the submission are as follows:

  • The technical proposal along with the CVs of key personnel of the team.
  • Organization Documents (in case of firm)
  • Financial proposal
  • Cover letter expressing interest and potentiality for the final evaluation.
  • PAN/VAT certificate.

10. Ethical Considerations, Safeguarding, and Child Protection

The evaluation must fully comply with the ethical, safeguarding, and child protection policies of Forward Looking and Felm. The evaluator is responsible for ensuring the safety, dignity, and voluntary participation of all individuals, with particular attention to vulnerable groups such as children, persons with disabilities, and marginalized populations.

Key principles include:

Informed Consent: All participants must give informed, voluntary consent. For minors or individuals with limited capacity, assent and guardian consent are required.

Confidentiality: All information must be kept confidential. No identifying data may be shared without prior written permission. Any use of data beyond this evaluation must be approved by Forward Looking and Felm.

Do No Harm: Evaluators must avoid any emotional, psychological, or physical harm and ensure referrals to support services where needed.

Respect and Inclusion: All engagement must be respectful, culturally sensitive, and inclusive of persons with disabilities, psychosocial conditions, or minority backgrounds.

Safeguarding Compliance: Evaluators must complete safeguarding orientation. Any violation of safeguarding standards will result in termination of the agreement.

Data Protection: Data must be securely collected, stored, and disposed of in line with data protection laws.

By undertaking this assignment, the evaluator agrees to uphold these standards throughout all stages of the evaluation.

Intellectual property, Copyright and Ownership as well as use of findings

All data, reports, and materials produced during the evaluation are the property of Forward Looking and Felm Nepal. The evaluator may not use, share, or publish any content beyond this assignment without prior written consent.

Forward Looking and Felm Nepal reserve the right to use and disseminate the findings for internal and external purposes. Unauthorized use by the evaluator may result in contractual or legal consequences.

Obey of Anticorruption Policy:

Forward Looking is committed to the highest standards of integrity and transparency. As part of our strict anti-corruption policy, we do not tolerate any form of bribery, fraud, or misuse of resources. All consultants and partners engaged in the final evaluation are required to adhere to FL’s anti-corruption guidelines, ensuring that all activities are conducted ethically and in compliance with our core values. Any suspicion or evidence of corruption must be reported immediately. FL promotes a culture of accountability and expects all evaluation team members to uphold these principles throughout the assignment.

The tender can be rejected or the contract terminated if the contract arrangement or the implementation of the contract involve bribery or corresponding unlawful activity

description:
﻿﻿Terms of Reference (ToR)

For Consultancy Services on

Soil Testing of Agricultural Land

Background and Rationale:

Rural Development Centre (RDC) Nepal is a non-political and non-profitable organization established on May 2002 with its head office in Rautahat District, Madhesh Province, Nepal. Since then, RDC Nepal is heavily engaged in humanitarian assistance, community development, conservation of natural resources, and environmental protection mainly in the Terai region of Nepal through the dozens of humanitarian and long-term development projects reaching out to the children, adolescent, youth, women, landless, urban poor and people living with disabilities, HIV & AIDS patients, conflict and disaster survivors from the poor families of historically marginalized Dalits, Muslims, Madhesi and Indigenous communities and other underprivileged groups.

Throughout its journey, RDC Nepal has been recognized by the Government of Nepal, Donor Communities, UN Agencies, many International Relief and Development Agencies for its achievements in transforming the society, for its good governance, inclusive operating structure, result-oriented development interventions and humanitarian assistance, which RDC Nepal considers its greatest strength to take the lead in the social &development sector across the country.

For creating greater impact of its program, RDC Nepal has been working on advocacy & influencing on Climate Change, Disaster Management & another relevant sector. Since April 2025, RDC Nepal has been implementing Oxfam funded “Building Community Resilience to Climate Risks & Vulnerabilities (BCRC) Project” at Chandrapur and Gujara municipalities, Rautahat district, Madhesh Province, Nepal. While implementing the programs, RDC Nepal believes to build climate friendly environment through climate smart works in all the aspects. Climate change poses significant challenges to communities affecting various aspects of life including agriculture, health and livelihood and many more.

To support evidence-based nutrient management and improve vegetable productivity, soil testing is required across vegetable farms. This assignment aims to analyze soil samples from 95 farmers and 1 vermicompost sample to assess their physical and chemical properties.

Objective:

The main objective of this consultancy is to conduct laboratory testing of soil and vermicompost samples to determine key physical and chemical parameters, providing actionable data to inform soil fertility management practices.

Role or Scope of Work: 

The consultant/laboratory will be responsible for: 

  • Collecting the transported sample from the destination point delivered by the organization. 
  • Conducting laboratory analysis of each of the 95 soil samples and the one vermicompost sample for the parameters listed below: 

Parameters for 95 Soil samples: 

  1. Soil pH
  2. Soil Nitrogen (Total or Available, specify method)
  3. Available Phosphorus
  4. Available Potash (Potassium)
  5. Soil Texture (Sand, Silt, Clay percentage)
  6. Soil Organic Matter (OM)
  7. Electrical Conductivity (EC)
  8. Calcium (Ca)
  9. Magnesium (Mg)
  10. Sulphur (S)
  11. Boron (B)
  12. Zinc (Zn)
  13. Iron (Fe)
  14. Molybdenum (Mo)
  15. Manganese (Mn)

Parameters for 1 vermicompost sample: 

  1. pH
  2. Moisture 
  3. Organic Carbon (C)
  4. Total Nitrogen (N)
  5. Total Phosphorus (P₂O₅)
  6. Total Potas (K₂O)
  • Ensuring quality assurance during analysis. 
  • Preparing a comprehensive analytical report including raw data, interpretation, and recommendations. 

Deliverables:

1. A clear digital laboratory test reports for each soil sample and vermicompost sample. 

2. A summary report including: 

  • Overview of findings 
  • Methodologies applied for testing 
  • Interpretation of results with reference to standard fertility levels
  • Nutrient status classification (Low, Medium, High)
  • Recommendations for soil amendments and nutrient management 

Timeline:

The complete set of assignment should be completed by the end of October 2025. Lab reports and summary report should be shared by 28 October 2025. 

Responsibilities of RDC Nepal: 

  • Will collect the soil sample from the field. 
  • Transport the collected sample to the nearest areas of laboratory via local transport service. 
  • Review the lab reports and provide feedback incase required.

Consultant Qualification: 

  • Registered and accredited soil testing laboratory 
  • Proven experience in agriculture soil analysis
  • Trained personnel and modern analytical equipment
  • Capacity to deliver within stipulated time

name: Akasha Academy
description:
﻿﻿﻿﻿Job Offer: School Program Coordinator at Akasha Academy

 

Akasha Academy is currently looking for a School Program Coordinator at the Headquarters site in Suntakhan, Gokarneshwor Municipality.


About Akasha Academy

Akasha Academy is creating pathways for the future of our planet, based on Universal Ethics.

The establishment of Akasha Academy in Nepal follows the vision of Tulku Khyungdor Rinpoche to offer a place for integrated education, rooted in the universal wisdom of original Buddhism. On that foundation, the main areas of work include education, health and environmental protection. A special focus is set on the empowerment of girls and women.

The Akasha Academy NGO is a non-governmental, non-profit organization registered in Nepal. The NGO's constitutional goal is to contribute to a positive and sustainable development through environmental protection, health promotion, education, and respect for human rights. The Akasha Academy NGO has been successfully carrying out projects since its foundation in 2012.

Akasha Academy is working closely together with its German sister organization Long Yang e.V.

More information: https://www.akasha-academy.org.np/

 

Development of Akasha Academy Headquarters

The Headquarters of Akasha Academy is located at the border of Shivapuri National Park in Suntakhan, Gokarneshwor Municipality. It is envisioned to serve as a flagship project for sustainable land use, planning, architecture, and infrastructure. The master planning of the land with sustainable architecture and infrastructure is currently in the making. Akasha Academy also supports local food systems and runs a model farm for regenerative, organic agriculture in Suntakhan, offering healthy locally grown food as well as training for the local community in these fields.

Akasha Education

In view of the current global and local developments, it has become increasingly clear that there is a need to support especially the younger generation in being able to meet today's challenges.

This is how the vision of Akasha Academy as a place for integrated education in the fields of health and environment came into being. The aim of Akasha Education is to create conditions for young people from diverse backgrounds to find their path in life and give them the necessary tools to face the current challenges globally and locally. Akasha Education programs in Nepa currently consist of different workshops and the Akasha Traineeship, a vocational training for women.

Akasha Environment

The vision of Akasha Academy also includes ecosystems restoration, reforestation, enhancing the local biodiversity, sustainable land use and regenerative, organic farming principles as well as training for the local community in these fields. Furthermore, we engage the community in clean-up campaigns, plantation activities and through awareness campaigns. We work with the local government, public schools, women’s groups and small-holder farmers to contribute to a positive development towards healthy people and ecosystems in the area.

A new project, starting from November will combine education and environment and focus on an awareness program on environmental and climate change education for 16 public schools in Gokarneshwor Municipality.

 

Role of the position

The role of the School Program Coordinator will focus mainly on the coordination of workshops and activities in collaboration with all 16 public schools of Gokarneshwor Municipality as well as the coordination of curriculum and content development. For the position, daily presence at the premises in Suntakhan (Gokarneshwor) will be required. The ideal candidate would be ready to relocate or stay nearby during the working week.  

 

Contract period

Initially 1 year, with the possibility of extension; long-term engagement envisioned

 

Tasks and responsibilities:

·       Coordination of various activities and regular events with all 16 schools of Gokarneshwor Municipality

·       Preparing and organizing the development of a curriculum for the school program related to environmental protection and climate change adaptation in line with the organization’s education approach

·       Coordination and communication with different government stakeholders, school management committees, and other working partners of Akasha Academy

·       Supervision and coordination of assistant trainers of the school program

·       Monitoring and reporting on progress related to the project, ensuring to keep agreed upon timelines,

·       Represent the organization at relevant events, support in expanding the network to relevant public and private stakeholders

·       Further develop the program according to the larger vision of the organization, support in proposal development

·       Regular travel and visits to all 16 public schools of the municipality

 

Required skills and experience:

Bachelor's, preferably Master’s Degree or Diploma in relevant discipline, i.e. education, social work, project management, environmental sciences, etc.

At least 3 years work experience in the education and/or development sector, in one or more of the following areas: education, environmental protection and awareness, climate change adaptation, youth empowerment, or similar

Proven experience in leadership, project management and coordination,

proven experience in working with children and youth 

sound knowledge on child safeguarding 

excellent communication and presentation skills,

be courageous, curios and innovative

the capability to manage schedules of multiple topics and to manage unexpected situations calmly and in a flexible way,

solid command of Nepali and English languages, both written and verbal,

the ability to work within a team of different social and cultural backgrounds,

reliability and loyalty,

the aspiration to contribute to a positive change in local communities and beyond,

a strong identification and commitment towards the overall project aim and the work of Akasha Academy NGO,

solid command of MS Office package (especially Powerpoint, Word, Excel)

driver’s license (Two wheeler)

 

Ideally, you have

-          practical leadership experience in similar setting

-          strong network and advocacy skills

-          experience in education and coordination with schools, government and community stakeholders

 

Candidates interested in working with Akasha Academy NGO are requested to send their complete application, including CV, motivation letter and expected salary in English language, to hr(at)akasha-academy.org until 23.10.2025. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the advertisement might be closed prior to the deadline, if suitable candidates apply.

 

In case of questions, do not hesitate to contact us. We are looking forward to hearing from you.
